clauses.statement: The edge example requires and exercises Fetch, response streams, `AbortController`, `TextDecoder` and WebCrypto.
clauses.ablation: M9 S6: each capability is REMOVED from the global object in its own child process, before the worker's module graph is imported, and the request must then fail rather than render. Seven rows red (TextDecoder, TextEncoder, ReadableStream, Response, Request, AbortController, AbortSignal); WebCrypto fails CLOSED with the library's own DigestUnavailableError; removing global `fetch` with NO injected transport changes the failure from `fetch failed` to `transport is not a function`. The control renders in the same harness, and an eighth row proves an injected transport does not hide the other four.
clauses.evidenceLine: The earlier NOT-PROVEN rested on the argument that a graph using neither `TextDecoder` nor `fetch` 'would fail to run at all rather than fail a named test' — which is an argument that the property is untestable, and it was wrong: it is testable by removing the capability and requiring the failure. ATTRIBUTION IS STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the WebCrypto row belongs unambiguously to `lokalized/load` and the `fetch` row to the worker's own `env.fetch ?? fetch`; the other rows are attributed to the DEPLOYMENT, because with `ReadableStream` absent a `Response` cannot carry a body at all and no probe can separate worker from loader from transport.

clauses.slice: M-D S22 (the browser property both clauses were held on, measured)
clauses.ablation: Seven ablations, all firing, control clean — and J1 is the mutation the BROWSER control actually measured. Dropping `crossorigin` from the emitted preload reds 'their attribute set is the one the browser measurement was taken against'; adding an `integrity` attribute reds that and the integrity test; changing `as="fetch"` to `as="script"` reds the attribute set; changing the loader's default to `credentials: "include"` reds the anonymous-mode test. Three more attack the RECORD rather than the code: removing its control arm, recording that control arm as 1 (reused, so it controls nothing), and recording a matched arm as 2 each red 'it carries a control arm that was NOT reused'. A behaviour-preserving comment is exit 0.
clauses.evidenceLine: CLOSED by M-D S22, in a real browser. Plan 6.3:2179-2183 names four things that must match for a preload to be reused; three were already checked in Node and the fourth — whether the browser genuinely reuses the entry — is what both clauses were held on. Measured on Chrome 152 over a trustworthy origin, with the preloads observed to have landed (4 of 4) before the loader ran so a reuse cannot be confused with a race: the three MATCHED urls produce ONE performance.getEntriesByType('resource') entry each, initiator `link`, no 'fetch' entry at all. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THAT READABLE: a fourth url preloaded WITHOUT `crossorigin`, so its CORS mode does not match the loader's, produces TWO entries with initiators `link+fetch` — and Chrome names the cause itself ('is found, but is not used because the request credentials mode does not match'), while emitting no such warning for the three matched urls. Recorded in measurements/preload-reuse.json with the attribute set it was taken against; test/preload-reuse.test.js is the half that runs without a browser and GATES on that attribute set moving, on the deterministic-and-machine-independent reasoning scenario:2k uses for its catalog digest rather than 0a's report-only rule for source graphs.

clauses.statement: The pinned IANA/JDK-compatibility closure is generated from a registry snapshot recording `File-Date` and source SHA-256, with explicit JDK-compatibility override rows.
clauses.slice: A30 (the generation direction is registry -> artifact: lokalized-spec tools/iana-oracle/generate.mjs)
clauses.ablation: A30 (2026-09-23). SPEC SIDE, measured by the spec builder in fresh throwaway copies with clean controls (recorded in its report): check:iana-registry (no JDK) refuses or reds on deleting yol's `Preferred-Value: enm` (368 classes / 779 tags, below the 781 floor, fingerprint moves), a moved File-Date, an emptied or truncated compatibility row list, a duplicated or unknown-keyed row, a script record given a Preferred-Value, a hand-edited artifact, IANA-PROVENANCE.md or lock, and a stale JDK-check record or tool digest; check:iana (pinned JDK) reds on a moved or swapped pair, a reversed or truncated class, a dropped class, the model's nested step removed, and lokalized-java's registry arm replaced by LanguageRange.parse (26 mismatches, exactly the JDK-21-absent tags). JS SIDE, measured here in throwaway copies with a clean control: a hand edit to a generated module -> gen-iana-data --check and test/generated-data.test.js red; the artifact given a one-way region/variant pair -> gen-iana-data refuses; the artifact given a class ['no','zzz'] -> refused with 2 shadow hazards (no-bok dropped under a kept `no`); the mgp class dropped from the full module -> gen-iana-data --check red, test/negotiate.test.js red, conformance 3 FAILED; the fingerprint recomputation fed the lock's artifacts unprojected (inputsSha256 kept) -> test/runtime-metadata.test.js red. Before A30: CORRECTED 2026-09-22: the claim that reconstruction is two-sided and that 'a missing row leaves a difference' is false, measured — overrides are computed as the difference, so the reconstruction cannot fail. Before: Reconstruction IS the check and it is two-sided: applying all 156 overrides to the registry-derived closure must reproduce the JDK artifact byte-identically, and an override that changes nothing is reported. A missing row leaves a difference; a padded row is named. Re-derived on every `npm run check`. Measured while building it: Corretto 27 yields 812 entries against 21's 806 — six added (dyl, enm, sgn-dyl, sgn-zhk, yol, zhk), zero changed, zero removed — and zero corpus cases touch any of them. VERDICT PASS (independent, 2026-09-23, throwaway copies, each restored and re-controlled): F1 swapping the Subtag lines of the gfx and mwj registry records -> check:iana-registry red; F2 the same, then generate --write -> the generated class order moves ([vaj, mwj, gfx, oun]), lokalized-java's independent derivation disagrees (check:iana red) and every JS consumer reds; G jdk-compatibility.json rows 9/10 swapped (-alalc97 before -heploc), then regenerated -> check:iana red; H the same swap unregenerated -> check:iana-registry red; J the JS generator sorting each class's non-root members, unwritten -> gen-iana-data --check red ('on-disk bytes differ'); J2 the same edit WRITTEN -> gen-iana-data --check exit 0 and test/generated-data.test.js green, while test/negotiate.test.js 'IS the spec artifact' reds (36/37), test/iana-model-parity.test.js 358 of 131,461 and diff:language-range 344 unexplained -- so the verbatim property is gated by the last two, not the first pair; K one byte in the snapshot ('Sekele' -> 'Sekelf') -> test/runtime-metadata.test.js red. THE FOLLOW-UP OF 2026-09-23 closed the two order rules the pass found ungated: the root LAST in the 332 two-member classes, and the class sort reversed, each passed check:iana-registry AND check:iana once iana:generate --write and iana:jdk-check --write had re-recorded them (measured again: both exit 0); ../lokalized-spec/scripts/validate-artifacts.mjs (check:schemas) now reds on each, naming the class, and its pre-follow-up version stays green on both.
clauses.evidenceLine: PROVEN AS WRITTEN (independent pass, A30 resolution 11, 2026-09-23); no amendment is needed. THE DIRECTION IS REGISTRY -> ARTIFACT: ../lokalized-spec/tools/iana-oracle/generate.mjs, with NO JDK (it passes under `env -i`), reads the pinned snapshot (tools/iana-oracle/language-subtag-registry.txt, File-Date 2026-09-17, 9,296 records, sha256 755fad43...) and ONE authored input, tools/iana-oracle/jdk-compatibility.json, and emits generated/iana-language-equivalences.json (369 classes / 781 tags / 14 pairs), which records registry.fileDate and registry.sha256, and the format-2 lock whose ianaDataFingerprint 87b3a43b... recomputes from plan :1680-1682's projection. THE 'EXPLICIT JDK-COMPATIBILITY OVERRIDE ROWS' are jdk-compatibility.json's 14 ordered region/variant pairs: explicit, source-labelled (one label for the block: JDK 21.0.11 regionVariantEquivMap iteration order), a lock input, hashed as compatibilityOverridesSha256 4ce249f3...; the generator refuses a pair set that differs from the registry's. There are no rows for the twelve membership differences from JDK 21, because A30 adopts the registry's answer as the versioned 1.1.0 change; they are recorded as jdkParseDiffers (26 probes) -- M9-PLAN's 'where snapshot and JDK disagree' elaboration is superseded by A30, not a gap in this text -- and 'closure' now names the class artifact A30 resolution 1 renamed. WHAT EACH GATE PROVES: generate.mjs (check:iana-registry; spec check and CI) regenerates the artifact, the lock and IANA-PROVENANCE.md from the snapshot and compares bytes, and its record arm binds the JDK check's record generated/iana-jdk-check.json (current artifact and tool digests, zero mismatches, the probe space and the model's refusal count re-derived, JDK 21, the library's pair order equal, a non-zero count of JDK differences, and the corpus's librarySourcesSha256). ../lokalized-spec/scripts/validate-artifacts.mjs (check:schemas; CI) is a SECOND READER of the snapshot sharing no code with the generator: classes pairwise disjoint and sorted bytewise by member 0, member 0 the one member no record deprecates, every other member deprecated, every deprecated language-namespace tag in some class -- the two order rules no other gate could see. build.mjs (check:iana, pinned JDK) holds lokalized-java's independently derived table to the artifact key for key with order, its pairs and JDK 21's regionVariantEquivMap to the authored order (the rows' source label verified, not trusted), and its parse to the model over 116,658 probes. tools/gen-iana-data.js with test/generated-data.test.js proves the JS modules are CURRENT with the generator -- NOT that they are verbatim (ablation J2). test/negotiate.test.js ('IS the spec artifact') proves the decoded table IS the artifact and test/iana-model-parity.test.js holds the port's parse to the model over 131,461 probes: together they gate verbatim consumption. test/runtime-metadata.test.js recomputes ianaDataFingerprint from the lock's projection and re-hashes the artifact, the snapshot and the compatibility input. The old 130-row override table and the probed 818-entry closure are retired. Before A30: CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (M-R S24), by a seven-agent workflow in private copies whose central numbers two adversarial verifiers reproduced independently. THREE STATEMENTS BELOW ARE NO LONGER TRUE. (1) The override table holds 130 rows (81 order-only, 37 JDK-only, 12 membership, 0 registry-only), not 156. (2) The closure is generated by probing lokalized-java 3.1.0's OWN table on JDK 21 (build.mjs library mode, source 'lokalized-java'), not the JDK's; editing the spec's registry copy leaves `check:iana` current with an unchanged fingerprint, because that copy is not one of its inputs. (3) 'Proven by reconstruction' is CIRCULAR: each override row is defined as the difference from the shipped table, so reconstruction succeeds for any table — a class reordered to an arbitrary order still printed 'reproduces: yes'. `check:iana-registry` is not blind to every registry edit (its family counts and recorded-table comparison catch some), but the reconstruction is not the evidence it was described as. THE CLAUSE STAYS NOT-PROVEN, and the flip that would close it is now priced: every JDK-looking input is derivable from the registry — member order is 'the member with no Preferred-Value first, then registry-record order' (781/781), the 12 JDK-absent tags are the registry read as of JDK 21's bundled date 2025-05-15, and the 14-pair region/variant order is Java HashMap order over the registry's 7 pairs — so a JDK-free generator reproduces Java's table byte-for-byte, the 818-entry closure order-exact, and conformance 2,166/0. Awaiting the maintainer (planning/M-R-STATUS.md, M-R S24). Before: RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-19 from DEFERRED, because the ground it rested on has gone: the clause ledger's own `ianaRegistryAxisAbsent` predicate fired on the first run after the snapshot landed, which is the M-D S21 staleness machinery working as designed. EVERY ARTIFACT THE CLAUSE NAMES NOW EXISTS: `tools/iana-oracle/language-subtag-registry.txt` is the real registry (File-Date 2026-09-17, 9,296 records, 731,819 bytes, sha256 755fad43...), `generated/iana-registry-overrides.json` holds 156 explicit JDK-compatibility override rows (81 order-only, 37 JDK-only, 26 registry-only, 12 membership), and the equality is proven by RECONSTRUCTION rather than inspection. NOT PROVEN ANYWAY, and the gap is one word: the clause says the closure 'is GENERATED FROM' the snapshot plus overrides, and it is not — `build.mjs` still generates it from the JDK by exhaustive probe and the registry reconstruction VERIFIES that result. Those are different directions and this project does not close a clause by reading a weaker sentence than the one written. What would close it is small and is the maintainer's to authorise, because it inverts a documented decision: make `registry.mjs --write` produce the artifact from registry+overrides and demote the JDK probe to the check. The reconstruction already proves the two produce identical bytes, so the flip costs nothing in behaviour — it costs the property IANA-PROVENANCE.md argues for, that deriving from the oracle makes divergence structurally impossible.

clauses.ablation: M9 S5, seven ablations: removing the 256 ceiling reds 4; FIFO instead of LRU reds the re-touch test; the disabled branch caching anyway reds its own; a module-scope map shared across instances reds 4; not freezing the cached chain reds the freeze test in either branch. TWO DID NOT FIRE FIRST: keying on the caller's raw spelling (because `forLocale` normalizes at its own door, so the probe tested that helper — the raw option object reaches the key, and the mutation then reds) and the freeze (no behavioural test can see it, so the property is asserted directly).
clauses.evidenceLine: 3.4's memo is DECLINED PERMANENTLY on a measurement: instrumented over 1,440 lookups across 100 SSR renders, 80 edge preserve-arm renders and 60 redirect targets, the instance-locale arm it caches was hit ZERO times, so it is inert for the server/edge packaging the deferral cited. Plan 2.2:150's candidate-chain LRU was taken instead — 6 recomputations per SSR render over 4 distinct tags, 8.8% of end-to-end server time; memoized, supplied-match lookups 33,579 -> 3,738 ns (-88.9%). Conformance byte-identical at 2,117/0 across the change.
